chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A group of Muslims left on a journey and lost their way. They were overcome with severe thirst; they began using the earth for ablution and sought shelter under a tree. An old man dressed in white came to them and said, 'Rise. You have nothing to worry about. Here is water.'
So, they rose and drank until their thirst was quenched. They then asked, 'Who are you, may Allah have mercy on you?'

He said, 'I am of the Jinn who paid allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). I heard him saying, 'A believer is a brother to a believer, his eyes and his guide.' So, it is not right for you to perish in my presence.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of a believer being the 'eyes and guide' of another according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin* illustrates the cosmic dimension of *al-mu'min akhu al-mu'min* (the believer is the brother of the believer), extending the concept of mutual guidance beyond human interaction to include the Jinn who acknowledged the Prophet's authority. It highlights the practical implication that a believer's presence serves as a safeguard against loss or hardship, a principle rooted in the Quranic verse 4:114 regarding those who facilitate peace and guidance.
